items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In North Africa, the Middle Stone Age (MSA) has been associated with the emergence and evolution of
                    <jats:italic>Homo sapiens</jats:italic>
                    and is considered a pivotal period in the development of behavioral complexity. Recent archaeological discoveries have yielded a range of technological innovations, which are likely connected with ecological adaptations as well as new social and symbolic practices. Archaeological material from Aterian (MSA) contexts reveals early evidence for the key components associated with behavioral complexity, pushing back the first occurrence of phenomena such as symbolic use of marine shells, pigment processing and use, the production of bone and ivory tools, and shell fishing into late Marine Isotope Stage 6 (~ 150 ka). This paper reviews the literature and discussions on the Aterian lithic technology and use-wear studies in North Africa. Recent studies highlight significant developments in tool production techniques, and an increased variability within the Aterian toolkit. While reviewing and critically evaluating the available data and results, our synthesis highlights the importance of microscopic and use-wear analysis in studying technological behavior, regional adaptations, and tasks specialization within Aterian contexts. Integrating use-wear analysis with other approaches to the study of lithic tools provides new research avenues towards a better understanding of knowledge on the onset and consolidation of
                    <jats:italic>Homo sapiens</jats:italic>
                    behavior in North Africa and across Africa during the Middle Stone Age.
                  </jats:p>
items.summary: 《北非阿泰尔石器技术与功能研究：当前证据与展望综述》：该文系统梳理北非中石器时代阿泰尔工业的石器技术及使用痕迹研究，指出相关考古材料将海洋贝壳象征性使用、颜料加工、骨与象牙工具制作及采贝等活动推至约15万年前的海洋同位素阶段6晚期，并强调微观与使用痕迹分析对理解技术行为、区域适应和任务专门化的重要性，适合关注早期智人行为复杂性与中石器时代技术演化的读者。
items.title: Aterian Lithic Technology and Functional Studies in North Africa: A Review of Current Evidence and Perspectives

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Rudabánya II (RII) is a 10‐million‐year‐old fossil locality in Hungary that preserves a rich assemblage of vertebrate fossils, including specimens attributed to the pliopithecoid
                      <jats:italic>Anapithecus hernyaki</jats:italic>
                      . The RII dental remains of this stem catarrhine vary in mandibular molar morphology, particularly in the length and degree of tapering of the M
                      <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                      . The goal of this study is to quantify metric variation in the RII fossil pliopithecoid mandibular dental sample and determine if it exceeds variation in extant anthropoid taxa.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using a bootstrapping approach, we compared variation in RII pliopithecoid mandibular molar shape ratios and relative size to a taxonomically broad sample of extant anthropoids. We also used 2D geometric morphometrics to compare the occlusal morphology of the RII pliopithecoid sample with other fossil and extant catarrhines and explored the relationship between mandibular molar shape in the more sexually dimorphic taxa.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In many cases, the RII pliopithecoid mandibular molars are more variable in shape than the comparative extant samples when comparing ratios of linear measures and in geometric morphometric analysis. In shape space, the RII pliopithecoid mandibular molars are distinct from other pliopithecoids. Mandibular molar size is not related to shape.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We address two potential sources of elevated variation in the RII pliopithecoid sample: (1) a high degree of sexual dimorphism, which exceeds that of extant anthropoid species, and (2) the presence of two pliopithecoid species in the RII fossil assemblage. Sexual dimorphism is not likely to be the cause of elevated variation in this sample.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
items.summary: 《匈牙利鲁达巴尼亚晚中新世化石地点上猿类下颌臼齿的度量变异》：研究用自举法和二维几何形态测量学，量化该地点上猿类下颌臼齿形状比值与相对大小的变异，并与现生类人猿类及化石类群比较，发现其臼齿形状变异常高于现生样本，且下颌臼齿大小与形状无关，值得关注。
items.title: Metric Variation in Pliopithecoid Mandibular Molars From the Late Miocene Fossil Locality of Rudabánya, Hungary

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:italic>Molossus molossus</jats:italic>
                    , a species of neotropical bat belonging to the Molossidae family, has an annual reproductive cycle that includes two peaks of spermatogenic activity, one in April and another in September, and a period of total testicular regression in December. Although testicular regression and recrudescence are common processes in hibernating bats, they are rarer in tropical species, making studies on the hormonal control of these phenomena scarce. Thus, this study aimed to analyze and characterize the hormonal control and signaling of the processes of testicular maturation, regression, and recrudescence in
                    <jats:italic>M. molossus</jats:italic>
                    . Histological, morphometric, and immunohistochemical analyses were performed on the testes of animals in four phases of the reproductive cycle (juvenile, active adult, regressing adult, and recrudescent adult). The animals' blood was subjected to hormonal dosage for testosterone and estradiol. Our results demonstrate that the transition from juvenile to adulthood in
                    <jats:italic>M. molossus</jats:italic>
                    is characterized by enhanced steroidogenic activity in Leydig cells and increased testosterone production, supporting the establishment of complete spermatogenesis. Conversely, testicular regression is associated with reduced expression of steroidogenic components and androgen signaling, accompanied by decreased circulating T and impairment of Sertoli cell function, ultimately leading to disruption of the seminiferous epithelium and suppression of spermatogenesis. During recrudescence, the recovery of Leydig cell steroidogenic activity precedes the complete restoration of seminiferous epithelium organization, indicating that reactivation of androgen production is a critical event in the re‐establishment of reproductive function in
                    <jats:italic>M. molossus</jats:italic>
                    .
                  </jats:p>
authors: Emília M. Soares, Juliana F. Ferraz, Cornélio S. Santiago, Larissa P. R. Venâncio, Arlindo G. Macedo‐Junior, Sebastião R. Taboga, Mateus R. Beguelini
items.summary: 《蝙蝠Molossus molossus睾丸成熟、退化和恢复过程中的激素调控与信号传导》：该研究通过组织学、形态计量和免疫组化分析及睾酮、雌二醇激素测定，探究新热带蝙蝠Molossus molossus在幼年、活跃成年、退化成年和恢复成年四个生殖周期阶段的睾丸激素调控与信号传导，揭示从幼年到成年转变伴随间质细胞类固醇活性增强和睾酮升高，睾丸退化与类固醇生成…
items.title: Hormonal control and signaling of the testis of the bat Molossus molossus during the processes of testicular maturation, regression, and recrudescence

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Meissner corpuscles are rapidly adapting mechanoreceptors involved in tactile discrimination in human glabrous hand skin. Detailed information on their regional distribution and variation across age, sex, and hand side remains limited. This study mapped Meissner corpuscles in 17 phalangeal and palmar regions from 46 individuals (27 male and 19 female) aged 3–92 years. Corpuscles were identified by S100 protein immunoreactivity. Density, the Meissner corpuscle index relative to dermal papillae, and equivalent circular diameter (ECD) were assessed using prespecified morphometric procedures. Descriptive comparisons were made across 17 hand regions. For distal‐phalanx density, a secondary aggregate‐level analysis compared 20 matched means per age group (five digits × two sexes × two hands). Density was higher in all 20 combinations in both consecutive age‐group comparisons before 40 years and lower in all 20 in both comparisons after 40 years (exact two‐sided sign‐test
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     = 1.91 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−6</jats:sup>
                    ; Holm‐adjusted
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     = 7.63 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−6</jats:sup>
                    for each comparison). Sex‐ and hand‐side analyses showed no consistent directional pattern among the aggregate means (all Holm‐adjusted
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     = 1.000). The Meissner corpuscle index was descriptively highest in the 21‐ to 40‐year group, whereas ECD was higher in the 21‐ to 40‐ and 41‐ to 60‐year groups and markedly lower after 60 years. The study provides a detailed anatomical map and identifies a uniform age‐related directional pattern in the retained aggregate distal‐phalanx data. Because subject‐level observations were unavailable for reanalysis, the statistical findings quantify directional consistency among aggregate means and should not be interpreted as subject‐level inference.
                  </jats:p>
authors: Irene Amigo, Yolanda García‐Mesa, Patricia Cuendias, Jorge Feito, Olivia García‐Suárez, Iván Suazo, Zulima Fernández, José A. Vega
items.summary: 《绘制迈斯纳小体在人类手部的分布：性别与年龄相关变异》：研究用S100蛋白免疫反应标记46名3至92岁个体的17个指掌区域，评估迈斯纳小体密度、相对真皮乳头的指数及等效圆直径，发现40岁前各年龄组比较中20种组合密度均较高、40岁后均较低，而性别与手侧无一致方向性差异，适合关注触觉感受器解剖分布与年龄变化的研究者参考。
items.title: Mapping the distribution of Meissner corpuscles throughout the human hand: Sex‐ and age‐dependent variations

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Scientific research is a political enterprise, and is therefore susceptible to cultural biases. With its central role in understanding humans as a species, primatology is particularly vulnerable to this dynamic, requiring researchers to carefully assess both the influences shaping their work and the implications of their results. Here, I engage in this practice by critically examining the study of chimerism in callitrichid primates, a prominent model taxon in studies of human health and evolution. Chimerism, which refers to cells derived from two or more zygotic lineages within a single organism, is a defining feature of callitrichid biology. Chimerism also challenges the boundaries by which many biological categories are defined. Using the lens of queer monster theory, I investigate the relationship between the study of callitrichid chimerism and the conceptualization of callitrichid and human bodies, with particular attention to the role of “queer” sex and reproduction. I first discuss the origins of chimerism within biological discourse, showing how the biological chimera inherited “unnatural” connotations that continue to shape scientific research. I then examine how similar monster‐making practices surface in studies of callitrichids, arguing that patterns of omission and claims of exceptionalism serve to manage chimerism as a categorical threat. Finally, I explore the promises that callitrichid chimeras present as monstrous informants. I show that callitrichid chimeras can be used not only to expose the cultural boundary‐work structuring sex and reproduction, but to invite research practices that treat categorical deviation not as abnormal, but as evidence that these categories must be changed.</jats:p>
items.summary: 《论怪物与猴子：灵长类遗传嵌合体研究的酷儿化》：论文以酷儿怪物理论审视狨猴科灵长类嵌合体研究，分析生物学嵌合体如何继承“非自然”含义并影响科研，指出研究中的省略与例外论如何将嵌合体作为分类威胁加以管控，并探讨嵌合体作为“怪物知情者”暴露性别与生殖的文化边界，值得关注科学知识背后的文化偏见。
items.title: Of Monsters and Monkeys: Queering the Study of Genetic Chimerism in Primates
